_swfapi_depRenames_basis: fapi_modules.py 1.21.11 -> 26.1 (0.141.6+1.21.11 vs 0.145.1+26.1): six modules gone. fabric-key-binding-api-v1 is mapped in the base table. Three were renamed with their API (Fabric API PR #5060, checked member by member by gen_swfapi_renames.py): block-view-api-v2 is block-getter-api-v2 (blockview/v2 -> blockgetter/v2), item-group-api-v1 is creative-tab-api-v1 (itemgroup/v1 -> creativetab/v1), screen-handler-api-v1 is menu-api-v1 (screenhandler/v1 -> menu/v1). Two were dropped without a successor module, and this step's layer gives their API back: convention-tags-v1 (the v1 tag holders, whose tag ids live on in convention-tags-v2's data) and loot-api-v2 (its builders and source enum are loot-api-v3's under another package, its events are the layer's on top of v3's). A converted mod's range for the old id does not describe the provider's versions, so the range is any.
_swfapi_gamerule_basis: 26.1's Fabric API removed CustomGameRuleCategory, GameRuleBuilder.category(CustomGameRuleCategory) and the protected fabricCategory field (26.1 vanilla GameRuleCategory takes any id: register(Identifier), listed after the vanilla categories, headed by label()). The class is the layer's with 1.21.11's surface and bodies; category(custom) on any builder dispatches to a mod subclass's own override as 1.21.11's virtual call did, else runs 1.21.11's body with the custom category's vanilla stand-in (same id, registered once) in place of MISC; a mod's super.category(custom) runs that body; fabricCategory reads/writes the builder's custom category. The stand-in's label() is the custom name (CbFapiGameRuleCategoryMixin). The rule 26.1 constructs from that builder is tied to the stand-in and its own category() set back to MISC as in 1.21.11 (CbFapiGameRuleMixin); 26.1's edit-rules screen, which groups by category(), groups it under the stand-in (CbFapiGameRulesScreenMixin). Only where another mod already registered a category of the same id does the rule keep that shared category as category().

_swfapi_renderer_basis: 1.21.11 Fabric renderer entry points: 26.1 removed Renderer.render x2 / renderBlockAsEntity / getLayerRenderStateEmitter, FabricBlockModelRenderer, FabricBlockRenderManager, BlockVertexConsumerProvider and RenderLayerHelper (blocks tesselate through AltModelBlockRenderer into a QuadEmitter). The interfaces and helper are compat classes with 1.21.11's surface; rt/CbFapiRender runs Indigo's terrain-like path on 26.1's AltModelBlockRenderer and its simple path on the model's emitQuads (tint, emissive / maxLight, QuadView.buffer per chunk layer). A call through ModelBlockRenderer (26.1's does not implement the interface) reaches a mod subclass's override or 1.21.11's default; the BlockRenderDispatcher facade implements FabricBlockRenderManager. As 1.21.11's Fabric API overwrote them, renderBreakingTexture / renderSingleBlock (facade) and ModelBlockRenderer.renderModel (CbWallBlockRender) go through the same paths. The item layer render type getter (Renderer.setLayerRenderTypeGetter, FabricLayerRenderState.setRenderTypeGetter; ItemRenderTypeGetter compat) is kept on the layer and applied to the layer mesh's quads at its submit (rt/CbFapiLayerRenderTypes), where 1.21.11 asked it per quad at render time.

_swfapi_blockLayers_basis: 1.21.11 per-block chunk layer (ItemBlockRenderTypes' block table, BlockRenderLayerMap.putBlock(s)): 26.1 removed ItemBlockRenderTypes and gives every quad its own layer and item render type (MaterialInfo, from the sprite's transparency). BlockRenderLayerMap.putBlock(s) fill rt/CbFapiBlockLayers' table; a mapped block's model is answered by BlockStateModelSet.get as a wrapper whose collected and emitted quads carry the mapped layer and its item render type (terrain, moving blocks and block models all read the quad), and a mapped block's block item renders its item-model quads the same way (CuboidItemModelWrapper.update). Leaves keep 1.21.11's precedence (cutout-leaves flag, set by the level renderer and settable by setCutoutLeaves, read by the section compiler). ItemBlockRenderTypes is given back as facade/ItemBlockRenderTypes over the same table; an unmapped block answers the layer its 26.1 model renders in.
_swfapi_blockColors_basis: 1.21.11 BlockColor (one function of the tint index) and Fabric API ColorProviderRegistry: 26.1 replaced BlockColor with a per-block List<BlockTintSource> (one source per tint index; BlockColors.register(List, Block...), Fabric API BlockColorRegistry). BlockColor is given back as facade/BlockColor, ColorProviderRegistry as a compat interface whose BLOCK registers through BlockColorRegistry; rt/CbFapiBlockColors converts a BlockColor into a live tint list as long as the block's current models' highest tint index + 1 (26.1 reads that many; 1.21.11 asked exactly the indices the quads carry), an index past it still answered through BlockColors.getTintSource (mixin), and a 26.1 list into a BlockColor for ColorProviderRegistry.BLOCK.get. BlockColors.register(BlockColor, Block...) and both getColor overloads are instance redirects with 1.21.11's bodies over 26.1's lists.
_swfapi_submitBlocks_basis: 1.21.11 block submissions: vanilla OrderedSubmitNodeCollector.submitBlock(pose, state, light, overlay, outline) and submitBlockModel(pose, renderType, BlockStateModel, r, g, b, light, overlay, outline), and Fabric API FabricRenderCommandQueue.submitBlock / submitBlockStateModel (world, pos, state), are gone in 26.1 (blocks submit as BlockStateModelPart lists or meshes). rt/CbFapiSubmitBlocks: submitBlock submits the state's 26.1 block model render state, model to the receiver and special renderer to the storage (1.21.11's split); submitBlockModel emits the model (seed 42, empty world at the origin as air, as 1.21.11's renderer did) into a mesh submitted through Fabric API's mesh submission with tints r,g,b; the Fabric API pair emit in the given world and submit one mesh per chunk layer in the layer's render type (entity block layer / the caller's function), submitBlock also its special renderer. A non-vanilla receiver answers through its own override; super calls take the bodies above.
